tb-3B05-1.question:
A straight water wave travels towards a straight barrier (Fig a).

Which of the following phenomena of a wave can be observed in the figure?

(1) Reflection

(2) Diffraction

(3) Interference

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-3B05-1.reasoning:
Reflected waves are visible in front of the barrier. Curving wavefronts spreading around its edge into the region behind it show diffraction.

The incident and reflected waves overlap, producing the interference pattern seen in the image. All three phenomena are present: D.

tb-3B05-5.question:
A straight wave travels from medium X into medium Y at an angle. Its wavelength shortens in medium Y. Which of the following statements is/ are correct?

(1) The wave speed is higher in Y than in X.

(2) The wave bends towards the normal when crossing the boundary.

(3) The wave will bend more if the change in wave speed is larger.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-3B05-5.reasoning:
By v = fλ, since the wavelength in Y is shorter, the wave speed in Y is lower.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

Since the wave speed decreases, the wave bends towards the normal.

∴ (2) is correct.

By sinθ1sinθ2=v1v2, if the difference between v1 and v2 is larger, the difference between θ1 and θ2, will be larger.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-3B05-12.question:
A string is tied to a vibrator while the other end is fixed to a wall. A stationary wave of n loops is formed when the vibrator vibrates with frequency f. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) If the frequency of the vibrator is increased to 2f, the speed of the wave in the string will be doubled.

(2) If the frequency of the vibrator is increased to 2f, the stationary wave will have 2n loops.

(3) If the tension in the string is increased gradually, the stationary wave formed will have more loops.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-3B05-12.reasoning:
The wave speed is independent of the frequency.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

If the frequency is doubled, the wavelength is halved, and the number of loops is doubled.

∴ (2) is correct.

The wave speed increases with tension. By v = fλ, when v increases, λ increases, and the number of loops decreases.

∴ (3) is incorrect.
